🔻 Tehran City Council chief outlines factors behind capital’s wartime resilience 📌 Moscow, IRNA – Chairman of the Tehran City Council, Mehdi Chamran, has elaborated on the factors behind the Iranian capital’s resilience during the recent wars against Iran. Chamran, who is attending the 2026 International Municipal Forum in Moscow alongside a delegation of Iranian mayors and several members of the Iranian parliament, made the remarks during the international event. ​ In his address, Chamran highlighted the devastating impact of war on urban areas and the widespread repercussions the recent wars against Iran have had on the country's cities. ​ He stated, “The time has come for cities, rather than becoming victims of grand political games, to transform into bastions of stability, development, and tranquility for their citizens, enabling them to emerge from crises and continue their developmental trajectory with even greater strength.” ​ Commemorating the martyred Leader of the Islamic Revolution and the other martyrs of the imposed war, including the student martyrs of the Minab school, he described these tragedies as the result of the enemy’s reckless attacks on Iranian cities. ​ Urban resilience is no longer merely a concept within crisis management, but has become a strategic imperative for the survival and development of cities in today’s volatile world, Chamran further said. ​ Noting that smart governance and public solidarity are essential elements of urban resilience, he added: “Tehran’s steadfastness in the face of external pressures is precisely the result of this joint effort and civic participation.” 📲 @Irna_en ​

He said Iran has tied any agreement with the U.S. to an end to “all forms of aggression on all fronts,” starting with Lebanon. He called that condition a “tremendous sacrifice” by Iran that strengthens Lebanon.
